sourceNote: The T-pose polar bear mesh of the user, of 2026-10-24 (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist (polar-bear-arms.glb, tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py) and on each leg from the haunch line below the crotch to the ankle (tools/blender/polar_bear_legs.py). The user said: "now apply similar techniques to the polars bear" (2026-10-24), and "the bear's knee is still much bulkier than expected. it's not anatomically correct" (2026-10-27): long faces of the user mesh ran from the haunch to the heel, so the seated leg was a wedge with no hollow behind the knee. The faces of the paws, the feet, the trunk, the haunch, and the head are the faces of the user.
heatSourceNote: Each vertex that the leg rebuild keeps takes the bone heat of this mesh, the copy before the rebuild, and only the new leg vertices take the bone heat of the source (kept_heat() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Bone heat spreads over the whole mesh: with the heat of the new mesh, the weights of the crotch moved by up to 0.23, the seat top went 7 mm down, and a face of the left armpit and two faces of the right hip front folded in more samples (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).
paintedNote: The weights of the trunk, the head, and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py, and the new vertices of the legs take the automatic weights of Blender (tools/blender/polar_bear_legs.py). The vertices on the bones of paintedLower (the hips, the trunk up to the chest, the legs, and the tail) keep the rule weights. Blender weights on the legs sank the tail into the haunch and folded faces on the bench (branch rigify-polar-bear). Blender weights on spine and spine1 folded a V of faces on the lower back over the bench, and on the chest they cut a slit into the side of the trunk under each arm in the play.

rootNormals.note: The faces behind each knee joint of the source, within knee units of it, and in front of it, within kneeFront units, on the leg bones for at least half of their weight, take the normals of the skin with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The bent knee folds the back of the knee into a crease, and the front of the right knee keeps short ring edges that turn up to 58 degrees, more than the crease angle of the app (40 degrees). With the skin normals, these edges shade soft. No vertex moves (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the three rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts). They replace upperTwist.

name: Polar Bear

app.note: 0.8803 of the scale of the polar bear of 2026-10-24 (1.63455 m for each unit then, 1.4389 m now). On 2026-10-27 the bench went up to 0.38 m, and the user chose to keep the seated size: the head top of 1.50 m in the play of the hold before the higher bench (docs/decisions/2026-10-27-polar-bench.md). The leg factor and the shin factor raise the standing shoulder joints from 0.725 u, and the landmark rises with them, so that the trunk, the head, and the arms keep their meters. The reach is the reach of the arm factor below.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh (user rule: keep the limbs of a mesh of the user, and fit the props).
legFactorNote: The user chose longer legs with the size kept for the polar bear mesh on 2026-10-22 ("Longer legs, keep size"), because with short legs the round belly hid the lap on the bench, and the seated bear read almost as standing (docs/research/2026-10-22-polar-legs.md). The T-pose mesh has short legs too, so it keeps the factor 1.6.
shinFactorNote: The shins are 3.208 times as long as on the mesh, and the thighs keep the leg factor 1.6. With level thighs, vertical shins, and flat feet, the bench top is 0.38 m, as the side view of polar-bear-views.png shows against the head top. The user chose this bench of three variants (0.30, 0.34, 0.38 m) on 2026-10-27 (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-bench.md). The knee keeps its form: the stretch moves the points of the shin along the bone only.
jointsNote: The places are in the units and the axes of the studio in the pose of the source: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The probes are in docs/research/2026-10-24-polar-bear-tpose/. The legs part below the crotch at y 0.20. The thigh joint lies inside the haunch at y 0.28, as on the polar bear mesh of 2026-10-22, the knee at y 0.15, and the ankle at the narrowest leg cut. With the thigh joint at the crotch, the thigh was too short to sit level, and the seat rule pulled the rump down 44 cm. The neck is narrowest at y 0.63, and the head starts at y 0.79. The arms are in a T-pose: each round arm goes out level at y 0.73, free of the trunk beyond x 0.145 (sections-x.txt). The cuts across the arm axis give its middle line (arm-axis.txt): the shoulder joint lies inside the root of the arm, the elbow at x 0.29, the wrist where the paw starts (x 0.435), and the forearm twist halfway between them. The finger joint lies at the root of the claws. The ears start at y 0.96, and a ball tail sits at y 0.26 to 0.33 behind the rump. In the T-pose, the palm faces down.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind pose to the source, and the right side mirrors it: the thighs level and 15 degrees out, and the shins vertical, so that the knee angle from the side is 90 degrees, as the side view of polar-bear-views.png shows (leg_turns.py of docs/research/2026-10-16-hip-open/ 0 15 0, docs/decisions/2026-10-27-polar-bench.md). With the thighs 30 degrees out, the knees did not show more from the camera of the stage, and the rest folded more faces. The trunk shares and the bind arms are the values of the other meshes. A forward lean of the bind (open -12 or -18) folded both arms in each play sample, so the trunk keeps the seat of the source, and the play lean of the hold leans the spine (docs/research/2026-10-22-polar-seat.md).

armFree.note: The arm of the T-pose is free of the trunk beyond x 0.145, from y 0.65 to 0.79, and the trunk there ends below y 0.53 (sections-x.txt). A vertex of the free arm lies beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, within radius of the chain of the arm joints, and above the floor.

line.note: The angle of the other meshes of 2026-10-23: a lower angle mixes the weights of long arm faces.

knee.note: Each vertex splits its weight of the thigh and the shin by its height: the thigh share grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, around the knee joint at 0.15. Thus each ring of the quad tube of a leg takes one share, and the dual quaternion blend of the knee (bind.knee) turns it by that share of the knee bend. Bone heat on the short thick legs gave the shin the front of the knee and the underside of the thigh up to the haunch, so the knee stood as a hump above the thigh (user, 2026-10-26: "the polar bear's knee is unexpectedly bulky"). Ramps from 0.09 to 0.21 and from 0.07 to 0.23 bent the whole short thigh tube and filled the corner behind the knee (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the rump stays on the bench and the thigh turns forward. With the ramp of 0.17 to 0.28, the hips held most of the thigh, and the seated thigh bent only near the knee. With this ramp, the thigh turns as one tube from the haunch to the knee, and the bench is 2.7 cm lower.

weights.rigidNote: The two thin faces of the front of the right hip, where the thigh meets the belly, take one mean of the weights of their 4 corners. One corner follows the right thigh for 0.75 and its neighbors follow the hips, so both faces folded in each play sample when the pedal leg turned. The rings of the old knee cut them before (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).
weights.note: Beyond the plane of armSplit (armFree), only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only. armTop starts above the top of the level arms of the T-pose (y 0.79): from y 0.68, it gave the top of each arm to the neck, and those faces folded in each sample. Each ear follows its ear bone above earBase. The short tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall). The rig has no cut and no split of the arms (user, 2026-10-23). Each leg has quad faces from the haunch line to the ankle (source).

flip.note: The values of the other meshes.

check.note: The values of the other meshes.

shift.note: The fur of the mesh is cream: Oklab lightness 0.896 and b 0.042 (dark-faces.txt), against the white of polar-bear-views.png and SPECIES_COLORS of the polar bear (#efeae0). As the panda rule asks, each fur face with a chroma from 0.01 to 0.02 and up, and a lightness above 0.5 to 0.6, takes 1.045 of its lightness and 0.3 of its chroma. The black nose, eyes, and claws keep their colors.

colors.note: The color shift of the polar bear mesh of 2026-10-22 moves the cream fur toward the white of the reference. With the dark limit 0.0037 of that mesh, 12.1% of the faces outside the eye and nose boxes were dark, and with 0.0015 none.

eyeShell.note: The values of the other meshes.

chair.note: The seat is the piano bench of the pianist (prop): it is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The front edge lies under the hip joints, where the thighs leave the haunch, and the back edge at the back of the haunch. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.23). The bench of the app fits the body: it holds the haunch, and its front edge lies under the level thighs (benchFitOf() of tools/studio-body.ts, StudioBody.benchDepth).

crease.note: 12 rounds: with the 8 rounds of the other meshes, the level thighs of 2026-10-27 left faces of the hips turned over in the bind (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-bench.md).

kneeCrease.note: The bent knee folds the back of the quad tube of each leg into a crease, and the faces of the crease turned up to 169 degrees from each other. The seam is each vertex of both a thigh face and a shin face on the inner side of the knee. Each vertex within reach units of the seam in the bind moves half of the way to the middle of its neighbors in each of 4 rounds, times a weight that falls from 1 on the seam to 0 at reach (knee_relax() and seam_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The hips keep their share, so the crotch keeps its place. With no smoothing, 37 edges of the left knee and 48 of the right knee turned more than 40 degrees, and the crease showed as dark flaps. 12 rounds left 13 and 6 such edges, but made the knee 0.115 units wide, against 0.131 in the source. 4 rounds leave 16 and 8, with the knee 0.126 units wide (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).

fair.note: After the smoothing, each vertex at the back of the calf, from 0.03 to 0.17 units down the shin from the knee joint and within 0.09 units of the shin axis, moves half of the normal part of the way to the middle of its neighbors in each of 24 rounds, times a half sine over the band (calf_fair() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The fair moves no vertex along the skin. With no fair, the back of the left knee had 12 edges that turned more than 40 degrees (hard_edges.py), against 5 with the fair. A band to 0.2 moved corners of the heel and thus the pedal foot of each pose (docs/research/2026-10-27-rigs3.md, docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).

sit.note: The values of the dog and the deer, with 8 rounds of smoothing: with 6, two faces of the hips stayed turned over in the bind under the level thighs (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-bench.md).

bind.note: Each vertex with a weight on both the thigh and the shin of one side takes the dual quaternion blend in the seated bind (bind_skin() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that each ring of the knee turns by its share of the bend and keeps its radius: the knee front rounds over the kneecap, and the back of the knee folds into a crease. The linear blend put the knee front on a flat bevel at 0.83 of the round of the leg, and the knee was 0.120 units deep on its bisector, against 0.148 in the source. The other vertices keep the linear blend, and the app moves the bind mesh with the linear blend (docs/research/2026-10-27-polar-legs-rebuild.md).
